input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Section 13 (continued at p0090-p0093) contains a Garman-side IP indemnity: Garman warrants it owns or controls all rights necessary and indemnifies Sparkling (and its officers and directors) for all Losses, including settlement amounts and reasonable legal fees, arising from breach of that warranty, backed by the usual infringement remedies (procure the right, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify). There is no reciprocal or one-way Sparkling indemnity for Garman's software, and no customer-side exclusions (modifications, combinations, specifications) have been carved out, so the scope is actually broader than the fallback. Section 15's limitation of liability expressly "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14," so the indemnity is not swallowed by any cap or the consequential-damages exclusion. This sits at or above the playbook fallback and is not redlined. Sub-elements short of preferred, noted only: there is no express duty to "defend" or to control the defence, no refund remedy, the indemnity does not extend to breach of law, Garman-caused data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and the ten-calendar-day claim notice period is tighter than we would normally accept. These are points we may raise commercially rather than material failures of the rule.
